title: Peer desk check
note: Hand-placed. Each card uses the page’s date. Silent is —, not Neutral. Does not vote.

houses.name: Apollo / Torsten Sløk
houses.title: Is an Agentic Bank Run Coming?
houses.vsClause: A what-if about household cash. They did not read Liquidity, Rates, Growth, Inflation, or Risk.
quotes: Muse and similar agentic AI assistants could soon sweep household cash automatically into accounts paying 3.3% to 5.0%, instead of the 0.1% national average on checking accounts.

If every household used AI agents to optimize the return on their cash balances, banks could lose a large share of the cheap deposits they rely on to make loans, which would be a problem for the entire financial system.

houses.name: UBS CIO
houses.title: How will Fed rate hikes impact markets?
houses.assets: Equities IN; fixed income Attractive, including medium- to long-duration high-quality bonds; cautious on the longest maturities and lower-quality credit
houses.vsClause: One more hike, not the market’s longer path. They still want equities, and they will add quality bonds but not the longest maturities. Today equities are out and the long end is in. They call underlying inflation moderate.
houses.quote: equities withstand such a shallow tightening cycle
quotes: But we expect only one further rate increase and believe resilient growth and robust earnings should help equities withstand such a shallow tightening cycle.
Investors should maintain diversified equity exposure and use the rise in yields to add selectively to quality bonds, while remaining cautious on the longest maturities and lower-quality credit.

houses.name: BlackRock Investment Institute
houses.title: The AI buildout meets the 5% world
houses.assets: US equities OW / IN; short and medium government bonds over the long end; selective credit, away from the weakest and the heaviest issuers
houses.vsClause: Same five, including scarce cash. They will not own the long bond. Today the long end is in, and equities are out.
houses.quote: We stay pro-risk and favor select credit for income
quotes: The Federal Reserve raised rates for the first time in three years, easing near-term credibility concerns as the U.S. 10-year Treasury yield crossed 5%.
We favor short- to medium-term government bonds on a strategic horizon of five years or longer.

houses.name: Goldman Sachs AM
houses.title: International Market Pulse
houses.assets: Equities IN; duration Neutral; selective credit; TIPS as inflation hedge
houses.vsClause: Growth and Risk-on align. Inflation leaning cold is their path toward ~2% by 2027, not a now-print. They stay constructive on equities, which are out.
houses.quote: We remain constructive on equities as exceptional earnings
quotes: We remain constructive on equities as exceptional earnings and strong corporate fundamentals drive returns.
US inflation continues to make progress and we expect core personal consumption expenditures inflation to fall near 2% in 2027.

houses.name: Citi Wealth
houses.title: Higher Rates Are Here to Stay, and Earnings Keep Pace
houses.assets: Equities IN; duration underweight, front end preferred; up in credit quality. NFCI still loose.
houses.vsClause: Still wants stocks over duration. Today equities are out and the long end is in. Up in credit quality lines up with high yield out.
houses.quote: we maintain a risk-on bias and an underweight duration
quotes: Against this backdrop, we maintain a risk-on bias and an underweight duration as policy rates move higher.
The onset of a hiking cycle is not a historically attractive time to buy duration.

houses.name: 22V Research
houses.title: Marking to Market the Post-Fed Market Outlook and Small Caps
houses.assets: Risk assets still fine. Do not chase small caps, retail, or transports.
houses.vsClause: Mild restraint and a benign slowdown, and risk assets are still fine. Equities are out. They did not say inflation is hot today.
houses.quote: mild restraint would not be a problem for risk assets
quotes: Since the Fed meeting, uncertainty in the bond market, based on estimates of 10yr term premium, is falling faster than the growth outlook, implying real EPS durability.
The cross-asset view is consistent with a benign slowdown.

houses.name: PIMCO
houses.title: A Recalibration, Not a Rate-Hike Cycle
houses.vsClause: One or two more hikes, then stop. Inflation pressures fade by early 2027. That path is not today’s leaning-hot print.
houses.quote: Our base case is one or two more 25-bp policy rate hikes
quotes: Our base case is one or two more 25-bp policy rate hikes in the next few Fed meetings, broadly consistent with market pricing.
By early 2027, the non-labor cost pressures that kept inflation elevated in 2026 – tariffs, energy, computer equipment – should be fading.

houses.name: Barclays Private Bank
houses.title: The debt and yield eclipse
houses.assets: Duration slightly below neutral (3–5y); long end vulnerable; BBB-/BB crossover IN
houses.vsClause: Resilient growth and hike pressure still line up. They want duration a little below neutral, around three to five years. Today the long end is in. Inflation on their page is less clearly hot.
houses.quote: maintaining duration slightly below neutral, at around three to five years
quotes: the latter should not only prevent the US Federal Reserve (Fed) from lowering policy rates for the foreseeable future but also add to pressure for probably two hikes this year
maintaining duration slightly below neutral, at around three to five years

houses.name: JPMorgan AM
houses.title: Global Asset Allocation Views 3Q 2026
houses.assets: Equities moderately OW (US/EM/JP); US HY OW; UST Neutral; long European duration
houses.vsClause: Page is still 9 Jul. Same hot skew, growth, and pro-risk. More dovish on the Fed than Rates Tight, and still overweight equities, which are out.
houses.quote: distribution of risks tilts toward an economy that is running too hot
quotes: the distribution of risks tilts toward an economy that is running too hot rather than too cold
We remain pro-risk, favoring U.S., Japanese, and emerging market equities, along with U.S. high yield.

agrees: Growth is still firm where they spoke. UBS says resilient and firm. 22V says the growth outlook has barely changed.
Risk-on is still the house call. UBS, BlackRock, Citi, Goldman Sachs AM, and 22V.
The front end is taxed, and the 5s are out. UBS has the 10-year at 5.16% and October hike odds at 64%, and still expects only December.
challenged: Equities are out. UBS, BlackRock, Citi, Goldman Sachs AM, and 22V stay constructive.
The long end is in. BlackRock will not own it. UBS is cautious on the longest maturities. Citi is underweight duration. Barclays wants three to five years.
Inflation is leaning hot. UBS says underlying pressures are moderate. PIMCO’s 23 Sep card still says the 2026 cost pressures fade by early 2027.
Apollo’s 27 Sep note is a what-if about deposits, not a reading. Liquidity is still mostly BlackRock’s competition for capital.

closest.name: BlackRock
closest.clause: Same five, including scarce cash. They will not own the long bond that is in today, and they stay overweight US equities.

scorecard.falsifier: A cool inflation print that kills the next hike while stocks and the long end bid together — or a further jump in long yields that takes earnings with it.
